question.text: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The frequency of oscillations if a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mi>m</mi></math> is suspended from the same spring is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Frequency of oscillation of a spring-block system is given by, f=12πkm

Therefore, for both cases, we can write

f1=12πkm and 

f2=12πk9m

Required ratio, f1f2=91=31
